_README: Website content for Shree Veer Vittal Mukhyaprana Temple, Maraballi. All content is authentic and verified with the temple trust.

temple.name: Shree Veer Vittal Mukhyaprana Temple
temple.tagline: Abode of Lord Shree Veer Vittal & Lord Shree Mukhyaprana
temple.welcome: Welcome to Shree Veer Vittal Mukhyaprana Temple, Maraballi. A sacred spiritual centre dedicated to Lord Veer Vittal and Lord Mukhyaprana, fostering traditional worship, religious ceremonies, annual seva, and community devotional activities.

trust.name: Shree Veer Vittal Mukhyaprana Trust
trust.description: Shree Veer Vittal Mukhyaprana Trust is responsible for supporting temple-related religious activities, annual seva arrangements, temple maintenance, and developmental initiatives.

about.intro: Shree Veer Vittal Mukhyaprana Temple is a place of worship dedicated to Lord Veer Vittal and Lord Mukhyaprana. Located in Maraballi, Honnavar Taluk, Uttara Kannada District, Karnataka, the temple serves as a spiritual centre for devotees.
about.activities: The temple is associated with traditional worship, religious ceremonies, annual seva and community devotional activities.
about.significance: Lord Veer Vittal is revered as the compassionate form of Lord Vishnu–Krishna who stands upon a brick, welcoming devotees with infinite love and grace. Lord Mukhyaprana (Hanuman), the foremost embodiment of devotion, strength, and selfless service, is worshipped for protection, courage, and spiritual strength. Together, worshipping both deities blesses devotees with steadfast devotion, peace, and fearlessness.

architecture.title: Traditional Hall
architecture.text: A traditional coastal Karnataka style hall with a sloping tiled roof and wooden pillars, built for devotional gatherings and ceremonies.

architecture.title: Sandhya Mantapa
architecture.text: The sacred Sandhya Mantapa rooftop, currently undertaking the Taamra Aachchhadana (copper roofing) development project.

architecture.title: Stone-Paved Courtyard
architecture.text: A serene stone-paved courtyard where devotees gather for religious ceremonies, bhajans, and community devotional activities.

architecture.title: Carved Wooden Sanctum Doors
architecture.text: The sanctum sanctorum is entered through finely carved wooden doors reflecting traditional coastal craftsmanship.

architecture.title: Silver Prabhavali
architecture.text: The sacred deities are adorned with an ornamental silver prabhavali (arch) and fresh flower alankara during poojas.

history.title: Temple History – Punar Pratishtha
history.description: The temple displays inscriptions recording two important religious ceremonies celebrated with deep devotion.

milestones.title: First Punar Pratishtha
milestones.inscriptionText: Recorded on temple inscriptions as the sacred First Punar Pratishtha ceremony, solemnised on Friday, 24 March 2006 (Parthiva Samvatsara, Phalguna Vadya Dashami) at 12:13 PM during Mithuna Lagna.

milestones.title: Second Punar Pratishtha
milestones.inscriptionText: Recorded on temple inscriptions as the sacred Second Punar Pratishtha ceremony, solemnised on Saturday, 21 March 2009 (Sarvadhari Samvatsara, Phalguna Vadya Dashami) at 10:40 AM during Vrishabha Lagna.

history.note: These historical milestones are inscribed and preserved at the temple premises, documenting the sacred religious ceremonies performed according to traditional rituals.

deities.name: Lord Shree Veer Vittal
deities.description: Lord Veer Vittal (Vithoba) is a beloved manifestation of Lord Vishnu–Krishna, traditionally depicted standing on a brick with hands on his hips, waiting with boundless compassion for His devotees.
deities.significance: Devotees pray to Lord Veer Vittal for pure bhakti (devotion), spiritual upliftment, family harmony, and freedom from worldly afflictions.

deities.name: Lord Shree Mukhyaprana
deities.description: Mukhyaprana — 'the chief life-breath' — is the revered name for Lord Hanuman in the Madhva and coastal Karnataka tradition, the ever-devoted servant of the Divine.
deities.significance: Worshipped for courage, inner strength, protection from fear and negative influences, good health, and success in virtuous undertakings.

annualSeva.title: Annual Seva Arrangement
annualSeva.intro: The temple invites devotees to participate in its annual religious seva arrangement.
annualSeva.description: The contribution supports temple worship and religious activities. Devotees who participate are included in the annual seva arrangement, under which worship is performed on a designated day every year.
annualSeva.significance: Participating in the Annual Seva provides devotees and their families a direct spiritual bond with the sacred ongoing worship of Lord Veer Vittal and Lord Mukhyaprana. Each year on the designated day, sacred pooja, alankara, and prayers are offered in the devotee's name for peace, prosperity, and spiritual well-being.
points: Supports ongoing temple worship, pooja rituals, and religious activities throughout the year.
Enrolled devotees receive the benefit of worship performed on a designated day every year in their name and on behalf of their family.
Devotees can enrol directly through bank transfer or UPI and share their details with the temple trust.

development.title: Taamra Aachchhadana (Copper Roofing Project)
development.subtitle: Copper Roofing Initiative for the Sandhya Mantapa
development.description: The temple has undertaken a development initiative to cover the Sandhya Mantapa rooftop with copper sheets, inspired by the devotion to Lord Shree Veer Vittal Mukhyaprana.

items.description: Procurement of high-durability sacred copper sheets for complete rooftop cladding.
Roof structural reinforcement, carpentry, battens, underlayment, and weatherproofing.
Artisan craftsmanship and installation labour for copper sheet cladding.

development.appeal: The temple trust humbly requests all devotees and well-wishers to contribute generously towards this sacred project. Every contribution, big or small, will help support the completion of the copper roofing work. May Lord Shree Veer Vittal Mukhyaprana bless you and your family with happiness, prosperity and well-being.

directions.text: The temple is located at Maraballi, under Jalavalli Post, in Honnavar Taluk of Uttara Kannada District, Karnataka.
Honnavar town is the nearest major taluk centre, well-connected by road and Konkan Railway.
Devotees travelling by road can follow the route towards Jalavalli / Maraballi or use the verified Google Maps directions link.
